taxonomyNote: Formerly treated as a subspecies of Eurycea longicauda (ADW still lists it as E. longicauda guttolineata).
fieldMarks: Tan to light yellow with three bold black longitudinal stripes from the eyes to the tail.
Tail about two-thirds of total length.
Underside boldly marbled black and white.
behavior: Mostly active at night, emerging to hunt insects and other small invertebrates.
Found under wood, rocks or other cover along streams and blackwater swamps.
Breeds in fall and winter; eggs are laid in underground crevices near springs and streams and attended by the female; larvae are aquatic.
habitat: Forested floodplains, ditches, damp streamsides, seepage springs, bottomland hardwood streams and cypress swamp edges; sometimes disperses into woods in wet weather.
range: Virginia and Tennessee south through the Carolinas, Georgia, Alabama and Mississippi to the Gulf Coast, including eastern Louisiana and western Florida; absent from southern Georgia, most of peninsular Florida and high Appalachian elevations. Not in Canada.

lookalikes.name: Longtail salamander
lookalikes.howToTell: Yellow to orange with vertical black bars on the tail rather than three bold body stripes.
